getting-started.speaker: Brimstail
getting-started.text: Hello adventurer, what can I do for you?

options.text: What's that cute creature wandering around?

steps.player: What's that cute creature wandering around?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Oh Izzie? He's my pet.

steps.player: What kind of creature is Izzie?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: I'm not sure. He's very cute though don't you think? It's very restful having a pet, especially when you are stuck in a cave for as long as I am!

steps.player: So, what do you do down here anyway?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Isn't that obvious? I investigate Thaumaturgy, I research the Arcane, I attempt to explain the inexplicable.

steps.player: You study magic then, what kind of magic? I do a bit of magic myself you know.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Are you a budding mage? I can tell you more about my research if you'd like.

options.text: Yes, that sounds fascinating...

steps.player: Yes, that sounds fascinating...

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Excellent, it's so rare I can find someone to discuss my researches, most gnomes seem to find it all very tedious.

steps.player: Never. How could they think that? Though, I suppose gnomes aren't known for their magic.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Well that's true. These days, apart from a few combat spells most gnomes seem to be a bit suspicious of mages.

steps.player: Really? Why is that?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Well there is a bit of history there, do you want me to tell you about it?

options.text: Oh, yes I love a bit of History.

steps.player: Oh, yes I love a bit of History.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Very wise, a good knowledge of the History of Magic is crucial to understanding the Arcane.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Well, the most famous Gnomish Mage of all got into a bit of .... trouble.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Most gnomes don't really talk about him. Other than telling stories about him as if he was some sort of boogie-man.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Ridiculous! He was a gnome like any other - he sounds like a fascinating character.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: He was one of King Healthorg the Great's advisors during the Grand Migration. But he was exiled after the Goblin Wars.

steps.player: Why was that?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Well, I'm not really sure. This was all before I was born - and no-one talks about what happened to Glouphrie these days.

steps.player: He must have done something very bad then.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Well, maybe? I'm not so sure. As it happens I've been looking into that part of our History. All I've managed to establish was that he was particularly interested in optics and light magic.

steps.player: It's hard to see what he could misuse light in a way that would get him exiled.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Well, indeed. I have also found though he was generally disliked by other gnomes - his moniker was 'Glouphrie the Untrusted'.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Oaknock the Engineer and Glouphrie didn't like each other either...

steps.player: Oaknock? I haven't heard of him before.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Ah, Oaknock was an engineer and architect. Very famous. There are statues to him around the place - his reputation amongst gnomes is second only to King Healthorg himself. He built most of the Stronghold you know.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Are you really interested in all of this? Do you want to see something interesting?

steps.prompt: Start the The Eyes of Glouphrie quest?

options.text: Yes.
No.

steps.player: Errm, not right now. I'd better go.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Fine! Humans really do prefer to live their lives in ignorance...

options.text: I'm more interested in your researches right now.

steps.player: I'm more interested in your researches right now.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Gah! Young mages these days. No patience. No perseverance. Magic is not a toy or a shiny weapon you know! You cannot alter reality unless you understand it. And you cannot understand unless you search for the true causes of things. And history is a record of the causes of things.

steps.player: I stand corrected - tell me more.

options.text: Actually I'd better get going...

steps.player: Actually I'd better get going...

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Well, I'd better carry on with my research then..

options.text: Err, maybe some other time.

steps.player: Err, maybe some other time.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Well, I'd better carry on with my research then..

options.text: Can you teleport me to the Rune Essence Mine?

investigating-the-next-room-talking-to-b.speaker: Brimstail
investigating-the-next-room-talking-to-b.text: Hello adventurer, what can I do for you?

options.text: We were discussing gnome magic...

steps.player: We were discussing gnome magic...

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Ah, yes indeed. Well I do have a little mystery for you. Has your curiosity been piqued?

options.text: Of course!
Actually, I'm a bit busy right now.
Can you teleport me to the Rune Essence Mine?

investigating-the-next-room-after-lookin.speaker: Brimstail
investigating-the-next-room-after-lookin.text: Hello adventurer, what can I do for you?

options.text: I've had a look in the other room now.

steps.player: I've had a look in the other room now.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: So? What did you find?

steps.player: There was a pit with a crystalline looking bowl in the centre.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Indeed, sadly I know very little about that, it looks elven to me though...

steps.player: There is also a large strange looking machine...

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: That's right. It was built by Oaknock.

steps.player: How do you know that?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: That room used to be Oaknock's workshop. I'd also recognise his style anywhere.

steps.player: What does it do?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: I have no idea. But I do know someone who might.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: There is one gnome left who knew Oaknock, and King Healthorg and Glouphrie for that matter...

steps.player: Who is that?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Have a guess.

steps.player: Errm....

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Well, King Narnode tells me you've already visited him...

steps.player: Err....
Oh I know, you're talking about Hazelmere aren't you?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Very good, young apprentice.

steps.player: Didn't he help create the Grand Tree?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: That's right. He was the third advisor to King Healthorg, he found and tended to the Grand Tree.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: If you are really interested in all of this, then could you do me a favour and visit Hazelmere for me? I've been meaning to go for a while, but I have responsibilities here - there's always someone who wants to use the Rune Essence mines.

options.text: Of course, I'd love to!

steps.player: Of course, I'd love to!

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Good! Good!

steps.player: Wait a minute, am I going to have to translate everything he says using that dictionary again?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Ha! He's an old fashioned kind of gnome and doesn't like visitors much. But I'm sure he'll want to talk about the Old Days.

steps.player: But he only speaks Ancient Gnomish!

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: That may be true, though he may just be faking it to deter visitors. Either way - he is a wise old gnome. If he really wants to talk to you I'm sure he'll find a way.

steps.player: Well alright, if you say so. What do you want me to ask him?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Well ask him if he knows anything about Oaknock's machine. And anything you can find about Glouphrie would be very interesting, wouldn't you agree?

steps.player: Right then. I'd better be on my way. I'll be back soon.

options.text: Actually, I'm a bit busy right now.
Can you teleport me to the Rune Essence Mine?

investigating-the-next-room-talking-to-b.speaker: Brimstail
investigating-the-next-room-talking-to-b.text: Hello adventurer, what can I do for you?

options.text: So where do I find this Hazelmere chap then?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: So haven't you managed to have a chat with Hazelmere yet?

steps.player: Not yet I'm afraid. Where do I find him again?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: He has a hut in a small island east of Yanille. It has a lovely sea-view, I'm jealous. I love my cave, but it's not very picturesque.

steps.player: Maybe you need some pictures. Though your pot plant adds something to ambiance of the place.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Oh, that's not my potplant. I think it was Oaknock's.

steps.player: Really? It's survived a long time. It must be a special pot plant.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: I suppose it must be. It shakes every now and again you know... I don't know why.

steps.player: How very odd. Anyway, I'd better get on my way to Hazelmere... See you soon.

options.text: Can you teleport me to the Rune Essence Mine?

discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.text: The mage starts to speak but all you hear is:

discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.player: Brimstail has sent me to ask you some questions.

discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.speaker: Hazelmere
discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.text: Ha! Atarischeray! Blah blah mesi blah blah.

discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.player: I have some questions about the old days. Brimstail has been filling me in about Gnomish History.

discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.speaker: Hazelmere
discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.text: Blah Brimstail blah blah human blah minahar!

discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.player: It sounds like a fascinating time. It also sounds like some important things happened then. Events that we shouldn't forget.

discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.speaker: Hazelmere
discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.text: Hmmph. Laquinay blah human. Blah blah blah.

discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.player: He has also found a machine - he says it was built by Oaknock...

discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.speaker: Hazelmere
discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.text: Oaknock! Ha blah blah minapor blah blah blah.

discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.speaker: Hazelmere
discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.text: Blah blah blah blah Oaknock blah blah blah.

discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.speaker: Hazelmere
discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.text: Blah blah blah blah Healthorg cinqo blah blah blah.

discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.player: Erm, I'm sorry I don't understand a word you're saying.

discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.text: The camera closes in as Hazelmere casts a mind spell on the player's head.
If the player doesn't have level 46 Magic:

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: ... ethereal link ... failed ... puny human mind ... insufficiently disciplined ... mental rigour required ... trained ... magical skills ...

discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.text: If the player has level 46 Magic:

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: Hmph. Not bad for a human.

steps.player: Weird! How are you doing this Hazelmere?

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: Old magicks beyond your skill human. You can stop flapping your big human lips as well. Just think.

steps.player: So how do I do this. Wow. That's impressive.  Brimstail was telling me that Gnomes don't trust Mages these days. Can you hear me? Glouphrie wasn't it? He did something bad and got exiled. Ooh, I'm feeling a little dizzy. You knew him didn't you? What can you tell me about him? And what's this machine that Oaknock built? Isn't that magical as well? Do you know what it does?

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: Stop wittering on [player name]. You're giving me a headache.  This mind speech is hard enough without having to listen to your incoherent babbling. Think about nothing. Clear your mind.

steps.player: Clear my mind? Hey, how did you know my name.

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: I'm reading your mind foolish human. How do you think?  Now CLEAR YOUR MIND...

steps.player: How do I think about nothing? I'll give it a go.
Hmm tasty lobster. Gah! I'm thinking about something. Stop thinking about Lobsters. Pink Lobsters. Big Lobsters. Lobsters with wings. Wings? Lobsters don't have wings. ARRGH. I can't do this.

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: Just shut up and listen! I have a story to tell you that will answer most of your questions.

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: Let us travel back in time, to the time you humans call the Fourth Age. King Healthorg had become King. The elves mysteriously decided to travel west, leaving most of Kandarin open for conquest. The humans weren't here yet, only King Healthorg and the gnomes to the north, and a collection of Goblin tribes to the south.
A map appears showing armies (flags) advancing towards each other

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: Both armies moved to claim the lands, and were of course destined to meet in battle...
A flashback begins, visually showing the battle between gnomes and goblins.

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: And so it came to pass the Goblins and Gnome armies met at the battle of Atarisundri.

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: Both sides faced each other on the Battlefield. A bloody battle was in prospect, our gnomes were brave, but we were no match for the mass of brute goblin stupidity...

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: ... but Glouphrie and King Healthorg had devised a plan...

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: ... If you don't lead an invincible army - pretend you do...
Glouphrie begins casting a spell.

steps.speaker: Glouphrie
steps.text: Em Gal lauf rei!

steps.speaker: Glouphrie
steps.text: Emeto Laufolly egramentos umesco lamiten gan!
A large group of tortoises appear behind the gnomes.

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: And so, Glouphrie created an army of illusory Giant tortoises, knowing that goblins would be scared of anything bigger than they were.

steps.speaker: Goblin 1 (unnamed)
steps.text: Big Boss didn' say nuffin 'bout de nomiez havin' monsta tortisses!

steps.speaker: Goblin 2 (unnamed)
steps.text: Dey be huges! Tortisses too scary and pointy. We runz away!
The two goblins flee the battle, soon followed by others.

steps.speaker: Goblin 3 (unnamed)
steps.text: Scarey tortisses! Runz!

steps.speaker: Goblin 4 (unnamed)
steps.text: Runz away!
The flashback ends.

steps.player: Hey! Was that you next to the tortoise? You look so handsome!

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: Handsome! Hmph! That was a long time ago...

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: Anyway, where was I? Oh yes...

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: Sadly, the golden times were not destined to last for long...

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: There was once a very special Spirit Tree in the Stronghold. Silver as a birch, old and wise - I considered him a friend. I called him Argento, his true name was unpronouncable.

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: He was the first Spirit Tree I had befriended, and the one I knew the best. I would sometimes travel, visiting and finding other Spirit trees, and during one such trip, I was filled with a great sense of foreboding...
Another flashback about Argento, the silver-coloured spirit tree, begins.

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: I felt a shadow pass over me, and a tingling in the air, even though the weather was fine and dry.
A large shadow appears and passes over the spirit tree.

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: Then I felt a sudden pain, as if the Anima Mundi was crying out with the loss of a favoured child...
A lightning bolt strikes Argento, splitting him in half.

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: And I knew that one of the Old Ones had died, and I had lost a friend.
The flashback ends.

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: I rushed straight back to the Grand Tree, only to find that no-one had noticed anything, and that Argento was still standing and seemed alive. But I knew something was wrong. He refused to talk to me and his aura was

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: no longer present.  Someone had hidden his death.  I talked to Oaknock and he was incensed.  He immediately blamed Glouphrie, and although Oaknock could be rather irrational when it came to Glouphrie -

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: they never saw eye to eye - I knew he was right this time.  Glouphrie had used his magicks to hide the truth from all of us.

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: Oaknock had made a machine - an anti-illusion machine, with some help from the elves.  He prepared it, and summoned the advisors to Argento..
A final flashback shows King Healthorg, Oaknock, Glouphrie and Hazelmere in front of an apparently intact Argento.

steps.speaker: King Healthorg
steps.text: Why have you summoned us here?

steps.speaker: Oaknock the Engineer
steps.text: You'll see sire. Switch the machine on!
The anti-illusion machine is activated, revealing the true state of the Silver Spirit Tree.

steps.speaker: King Healthorg
steps.text: What is the meaning of this?

steps.speaker: Oaknock the Engineer
steps.text: The Silver Spirit Tree is dead!

steps.speaker: Oaknock the Engineer
steps.text: Glouphrie has been using his foul arts to mask the truth! What other secrets has he been keeping?
The King turns to Glouphrie.

steps.speaker: King Healthorg
steps.text: Explain yourself!

steps.speaker: Glouphrie the Untrusted
steps.text: I live to serve you sire. I work for the good of us all.

steps.speaker: King Healthorg
steps.text: How can lying to your fellow gnomes be 'Good'?

steps.speaker: Glouphrie the Untrusted
steps.text: Some things are best kept secret...

steps.speaker: King Healthorg
steps.text: Even from your King!?

steps.speaker: Glouphrie the Untrusted
steps.text: Occasionally.

steps.speaker: King Healthorg
steps.text: Enough! How can I trust a gnome who hides things from me?

steps.speaker: Glouphrie the Untrusted
steps.text: No gnome can blame you for what you do not know.

steps.speaker: King Healthorg
steps.text: That is NOT how I rule.

steps.speaker: King Healthorg
steps.text: Glouphrie. You are no longer my advisor. Leave this place.

steps.speaker: Glouphrie the Untrusted
steps.text: Only the naive believe they can rule without someone like me.

steps.speaker: Glouphrie the Untrusted
steps.text: Your empire will crack and the gnomes will become but a joke.

steps.speaker: King Healthorg
steps.text: Sarko!

steps.speaker: Glouphrie the Untrusted
steps.text: So be it. I'll be watching.

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: And so Glouphrie left and travelled with some companions to a place they called Arposandra. We have heard nothing but rumours about them since...
The flashback ends.

steps.player: So where's this Arposandra place anyway?

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: Nobody knows for certain, somewhere rocky I suppose. The rumour is that after founding his new home, Glouphrie used his magicks to shroud the city in mist. Arposandra may not exist at all, however I suspect that

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: Glouphrie is still around, one way or another.

steps.player: Why do you think that?

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: Just call it Gnomish intuition.

steps.player: So the machine that Brimstail has found is the one that Oaknock built to stop Glouphrie's illusions.  Do you know how it worked?

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: I never studied it, but I believe it used elven magic - So it must have used crystals of some sort. Crystal discs, yes that sounds familiar.  Actually come to think of it I think I may have one lying around.  Here take

steps.player: this, maybe it will help you.

steps.text: Violet pentagon

steps.player: Well, thank you, Hazelmere. You've told me a lot of things I need to ponder for a while.

steps.speaker: Hazelmere
steps.text: Very well. Oh and when you see that lazy toad Brimstail, tell him next time he needs information to come himself.

steps.player: I'll do that. Farewell.

discussion-with-hazelmere-speaking-with-.text: The mage starts to speak but all you hear is:
The camera closes in as Hazelmere casts a mind spell on the player's head.

discussion-with-hazelmere-talking-to-haz.text: The mage starts to speak but all you hear is:
The camera closes in as Hazelmere casts a mind spell on the player's head.

discussion-with-hazelmere-talking-to-haz.speaker: Hazelmere
discussion-with-hazelmere-talking-to-haz.text: What do you want now? Go and talk to Brimstail, that's why you came to see me in the first place...

the-anti-illusion-machine-returning-to-b.speaker: Brimstail
the-anti-illusion-machine-returning-to-b.text: Hello adventurer, what can I do for you?

options.text: I've visited Hazelmere, he told me all sorts of interesting things.

steps.player: I've visited Hazelmere, he told me all sorts of interesting things.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Ah, thank you my young apprentice. What did he tell you?

steps.player: Right. Well it starts during the Great Migration...

steps.text: You tell Brimstail everything Hazelmere told you - Brimstail takes lots of notes.
A cutscene shows a near-invisible gnome sneak by Brimstail and the player as they discuss.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: So the machine emits an anti-illusion glamour?

steps.player: Glamour? What's that?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Don't you know anything? *sigh* A glamour is a type of enchantment or magical effect.

steps.player: Oh yes it does have such a glamour. It seems to use crystal discs to work in some way.

steps.text: You show Brimstail the disc Hazelmere gave you.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Oh, crystal discs? I may have a few of those in a drawer somewhere.

steps.player: What's that? Something just moved behind you...

steps.text: The gnome destroys the machine.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Really? Wait - what's that banging noise?
Brimstail and the player hurry up to the other room

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: What's happened to the machine? It's broken!

steps.player: Hmm, something is afoot.  I sense sabotage....

steps.text: End of cutscene.

options.text: Can you teleport me to the Rune Essence Mine?

the-anti-illusion-machine-speaking-to-br.speaker: Brimstail
the-anti-illusion-machine-speaking-to-br.text: Hello adventurer, what can I do for you?

options.text: The machine is broken, I suspect sabotage...!

steps.player: The machine is broken, I suspect sabotage...!

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: This is intolerable! How could this happen?

steps.player: I'm confused, it must have happened while we were here talking!

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: But we were just standing here, how could someone get past us?

steps.player: I did see something odd behind you...

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Wait a minute, how did the saboteur know about the machine?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Hmmm ... You're the only person I've told about the machine...

steps.player: Hey! Don't look at me like that. The only person I've talked to is Hazelmere.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Surely this couldn't be the work of Hazelmere... That turncoat!!

steps.player: Wait! Wait! None of this makes any sense. There must be another explanation.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Alright. Someone snuck in here without us noticing. How?

steps.player: The intruder must have been invisible.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Right, and how does one make oneself invisible?
If the player has progressed far enough into Monkey Madness I:

steps.player: Of course! I've seen this before. Karam in the 10th squad used some sort of magic to make himself invisible.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Do you think the 10th squad did this?

steps.player: No, but I think our saboteur must have learnt the same magicks. Is Glouphrie still alive?

steps.text: If the player hasn't progressed far enough into Monkey Madness I:

steps.player: Illusion magic?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Invisibility is a form of illusion magic. So that makes sense...

steps.player: So this was done by Glouphrie? Is he still alive?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Who knows, but he may well have taught the skills to his gnomes.

steps.player: You mean the gnomes that went with Glouphrie to Arposandra?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Right. And why would they sabotage an anti-illusion device?

steps.player: Because there is an illusion that they want to remain hidden?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Of course. Which makes it imperative that we fix this machine and find out what it is!

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Have a look at the machine and assess the damage. I'll hunt around my boxes and see if I can find anything that might help.

options.text: Can you teleport me to the Rune Essence Mine?

the-anti-illusion-machine-talking-to-bri.speaker: Brimstail
the-anti-illusion-machine-talking-to-bri.text: Hello adventurer, what can I do for you?

options.text: Something's happened to the machine! It's broken!

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Have you had a look at the damage yet?

steps.player: Not yet. I'll get right to it.

options.text: Can you teleport me to the Rune Essence Mine?

the-anti-illusion-machine-inspecting-the.text: You look at the damage done.   There are two main wooden parts that need to be repaired. It looks as if you'll need two types of wood; maple and oak, to complete the repairs. It also looks as if everything was stuck together by some sort of resin based glue that smells of pine, and contains flecks of grey powder that glint and sparkle in a
You think that you'll need some skill in construction (level 5) and the standard construction tools to repair the machine.
If the player doesn't have glue:

steps.text: You need something to stick all the bits together.

the-anti-illusion-machine-inspecting-the.text: If the player doesn't have oak logs:

steps.text: You need some oak logs to repair this.

the-anti-illusion-machine-inspecting-the.text: If the player doesn't have maple logs:

steps.text: You need some maple logs to repair this.

the-anti-illusion-machine-inspecting-the.text: If the player doesn't have a saw:

steps.text: You need a saw to repair this machine.

the-anti-illusion-machine-inspecting-the.text: If the player doesn't have a hammer:

steps.text: You need a hammer to repair this machine.

the-anti-illusion-machine-talking-to-bri.speaker: Brimstail
the-anti-illusion-machine-talking-to-bri.text: Hello adventurer, what can I do for you?

options.text: I'm still a bit confused about how to fix Oaknock's machine.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: So how are your investigations going?

steps.player: I'm not getting anywhere with these 'sticky runes'.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Hmmm, which runes would you think are sticky.

steps.player: Runes are runes! None of them are sticky! They're all round and disc-like and definitely non-adhesive.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Open your mind and think laterally. Thinking sideways is an important skill for a mage.

steps.player: Oh, all right. I'll give it a go. Well - air, water and fire and earth runes. There's nothing sticky about them.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: I concur.

steps.player: Mind and body runes. Again distinctly non-glue-like in any way.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Keep going.

steps.player: Nature and Cosmic runes. Once more distinctly lacking in any gooeyness. Bah! This is a waste of time.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Patience young apprentice. You are on the right path - just think it through and I'm sure it will become obvious.

steps.player: Maybe. What do I do with the rune when I find it?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: What did Oaknock do?

steps.player: Well it looked powdered in the glue.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: So there you go. What more do you need to know?
If the player doesn't have a bucket of sap:

steps.player: Well, I'm still a bit unsure about getting this glue.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: So, what do you know so far?

steps.player: It looked ambery in colour and sticky, smelt of pine and had flecks of silvery stuff in it.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: It smelt of pine and was ambery in colour, that sounds like tree sap. From a coniferous tree probably.

steps.player: Tree sap?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Have you never tried cutting a coniferous tree and watching the sap drip out?

steps.player: Err no.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Well maybe if you had, you'd know something about tree sap!

steps.player: So where do I put the stuff?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Hmmm, use your head! What kind of substance is this tree sap?

steps.player: What do you mean?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Is it a solid, a liquid or a gas?

steps.player: Oh, I see - a liquid I suppose.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: So where do you put liquids?

steps.player: Some form of container?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Right! I think you know everything you need now...

steps.player: Thanks!

steps.text: If the player has a bucket of sap:

steps.player: Right. I'll go away and think about what you've said.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: That's right, use your noddle, exercise your noggin, employ your cranium. Think, think, think!

steps.player: Now you're just confusing me more...

options.text: Can you teleport me to the Rune Essence Mine?

the-anti-illusion-machine-making-magic-g.text: You mix the mud rune powder into the tree sap. It looks sticky.

the-anti-illusion-machine-repairing-the-.text: You've fixed it! It seems to be working now, though it does appear to be locked.

the-anti-illusion-machine-after-repairin.speaker: Brimstail
the-anti-illusion-machine-after-repairin.text: Hello adventurer, what can I do for you?

options.text: I think I've fixed the machine now!

steps.player: I think I've fixed the machine now!

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Well done! You're almost as good at fixing things as a gnome! Who'd have thought?

steps.player: Though I still don't think it's actually activated. There appears to be some sort of lock on the front. I think I know what the discs are for though. There's a slot in the front that looks like it might fit a disc, and a
number.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: So what do you think the number means?

steps.player: I'm not sure yet. Maybe I should put a disc into the slot and see what happens?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: That reminds me, I found those crystal discs I mentioned before.
Red square and Yellow triangle

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: They are not quite the same as the one Hazelmere gave you, but they look similar in size and weight.

steps.player: They also look as if they might fit in the slots on both of the machines. Maybe I should try it out?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: I wonder if the different sizes and shapes mean anything.

steps.player: I've been thinking that as well, I shall ponder it some more.. I'll work it out.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: That's the spirit! This is all good training for the mind...

options.text: Can you teleport me to the Rune Essence Mine?

the-anti-illusion-machine-talking-to-bri.speaker: Brimstail
the-anti-illusion-machine-talking-to-bri.text: Hello adventurer, what can I do for you?

options.text: I can't work out what to do with these discs!

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Hmmm. Maybe all of these discs all have different values and you have to choose the right one in order for it to work?

steps.player: Interesting. But how do I work out which discs are worth what value?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: I'm not sure, but there will be some logic somewhere. Maybe if you look around the workshop you'll find some clues?

steps.player: I'll have a look.

steps.text: If the player has not received the three extra discs from Brimstail:

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Oh, I've been rooting through my drawers and I've found a few more discs that you might find useful.
three random discs

steps.player: Thanks, I'm sure they'll be very useful.

options.text: Can you teleport me to the Rune Essence Mine?

the-anti-illusion-machine-inspecting-the.text: The panel shows a diagram of boxes stacked on top of each other. The stacks are split into seven columns, with each column being taller than the previous. Each column is also a different colour. From left to right, the colours are: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet.

the-anti-illusion-machine-using-the-mach.text: You have not unlocked the machine yet...
You'll need to insert some discs and change them first.
You press the button. Not a lot happens...
Not a lot happens. Maybe you need to insert a disc first...
You cannot add more discs after you have exchanged.
The discs you put into the slot, clunk out into your hand.
You'll need to press either the exchange or cancel buttons to return discs.
You hear the machine make some whirring noises.
The discs shown in the window clunk out of the machine into your hands.
The front panel of the machine is unlocked! Well done.
The machine is still not fully operational.
The discs you have put in clunk out.

the-anti-illusion-machine-talking-to-bri.speaker: Brimstail
the-anti-illusion-machine-talking-to-bri.text: Hello adventurer, what can I do for you?

options.text: I think Oaknock's machine is now unlocked, what do I do now?

steps.player: I seem to have opened some sort of control panel.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: I wonder how it works? a similar way to the locking mechanism I'd guess.

steps.player: There seems to be more than one slot. Maybe I need more than one disc?

options.text: Can you teleport me to the Rune Essence Mine?

the-anti-illusion-machine-unlocking-the-.text: The machine is now fully operational. Congratulations!

the-anti-illusion-machine-unlocking-the-.speaker: Brimstail
the-anti-illusion-machine-unlocking-the-.text: Well done [player name]! I knew you'd work it out. I'll make a mage out of you yet...
The machine removes the cute creature's illusion, revealing an evil creature.

the-anti-illusion-machine-unlocking-the-.speaker: Brimstail
the-anti-illusion-machine-unlocking-the-.text: Izzie! No! There's something very wrong going on here...

the-anti-illusion-machine-attempting-to-.text: The machine is now working, you don't need to do anything to it any more.

assassination-talking-to-brimstail-after.speaker: Brimstail
assassination-talking-to-brimstail-after.text: Hello adventurer, what can I do for you?

options.text: Phew! I've got that machine working now. What do I need to do now?

steps.player: Phew! I've got that machine working now. What do I need to do now?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Well, it seems that Izzie was not so cute after all! How awful! How mysterious!

steps.player: So this was an illusion the Arposandrans went to so much effort to conceal? A pet. That wasn't cute enough.
Where did you find this one?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Izzie just wandered into my cave. He was cute and friendly so I kept him.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: He seemed very curious, and used to watch me do my researches. I liked the companionship – research is lonely work...

steps.player: So he's been keeping an eye on you while you do important magical research...

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: I suppose it has. I hadn't thought of it like that. I'm sure I've seen others of these creatures around the place...

steps.player: Where?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: I think King Narnode has one, and I think I saw one by the gates. And I'm sure I've seen a few more wandering around.

steps.player: In other words all places to keep an eye on what's going in the Stronghold...

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Oh my goodness. I think I'm beginning to understand where you are going with this.

steps.player: Yes, they must be spies. They are watching us with those creepy red eyes. And they must have told someone that we were working on the machine.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: So that horrible thing was listening to us all along. You'd better tell the King what's going on.

options.text: Can you teleport me to the Rune Essence Mine?

assassination-talking-to-brimstail-again.speaker: Brimstail
assassination-talking-to-brimstail-again.text: Hello adventurer, what can I do for you?

options.text: What should we do about these creatures?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: So this horrible thing is listening to us right now... Aargh. Get rid of it! Don't forget to tell the king what's going on!

steps.player: I'll get on it now.

options.text: Can you teleport me to the Rune Essence Mine?

assassination-killing-an-evil-creature.text: I've killed [number] spying creatures so far, maybe there are more to find...

assassination-talking-to-brimstail-after.speaker: Brimstail
assassination-talking-to-brimstail-after.text: Hello adventurer, what can I do for you?

options.text: What should we do about these creatures?

steps.player: What should we do about these creatures?

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: Have you talked to the King yet?

steps.player: I'll get on it now.

options.text: Can you teleport me to the Rune Essence Mine?

assassination-talking-to-narnode.player: Good day sire, I take it you've noticed that cute creature you had in here is looking rather different now.

assassination-talking-to-narnode.speaker: King Narnode Shareen
assassination-talking-to-narnode.text: Why yes! Do you know what's going on?

assassination-talking-to-narnode.player: I think I do. It's a long story but the short version is this. The Arposandran gnomes have planted these creatures as spies to watch what's going on in the Stronghold.
I have just reactivated a machine that was built by Oaknock that dispels illusions, and now these creatures true forms are revealed.

assassination-talking-to-narnode.speaker: King Narnode Shareen
assassination-talking-to-narnode.text: Glouphrie! Now we know what he has been up to all these years. Gah! Never trust a Mage.

assassination-talking-to-narnode.player: Well, I wouldn't go as far as that – it is only through Brimstail's and my researches that we have established this is going on.

assassination-talking-to-narnode.speaker: King Narnode Shareen
assassination-talking-to-narnode.text: Harumph! Well, all of these creatures must be removed, we cannot allow the Arposandrans to spy on us any more. How many of these things are there?

assassination-talking-to-narnode.speaker: King Narnode Shareen
assassination-talking-to-narnode.text: Well find them all and dispatch them now.

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again.speaker: King Narnode Shareen
assassination-talking-to-narnode-again.text: Have you found all of those spies yet?

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again.player: Not yet, I'm still looking for them.

assassination-killing-all-evil-creatures.text: You've killed all the creatures now, you'd better tell the King...

assassination-talking-to-brimstail-after.speaker: Brimstail
assassination-talking-to-brimstail-after.text: Hello adventurer, what can I do for you?

options.text: I've killed all of the spies.

steps.speaker: Brimstail
steps.text: That's a relief. Well, that's all good work, but I think you'd better inform the King now.

steps.player: I'll get on it now.

options.text: Can you teleport me to the Rune Essence Mine?

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.speaker: King Narnode Shareen
assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.text: Have you found all of those spies yet?

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.player: I think so. There were six in total.

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.speaker: King Narnode Shareen
assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.text: Thank goodness. Thank you for your help. Brimstail also tells me that you helped him a lot finding out what was going on!

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.player: Help? I did all of the hard work!

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.speaker: King Narnode Shareen
assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.text: Aha! Getting others to do the donkey work seems to be a skill that Mages develop well.

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.player: So what will you do now?

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.speaker: King Narnode Shareen
assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.text: Well, I have many things to think about. Why are the Arposandrans spying on us, and what are they planning?

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.player: It's certainly worrying, and whoever sabotaged the machine couldn't have been far from here. Are there gnomes here who are also spies?

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.speaker: King Narnode Shareen
assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.text: Indeed, that is another thing that worries me...

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.player: If you find out more I'd be willing to help investigate.

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.speaker: King Narnode Shareen
assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.text: That may well be useful. Thank you – I may well call for your help again.

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.speaker: King Narnode Shareen
assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.text: Oh, before you leave – I have something you might like.

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.speaker: King Narnode Shareen
assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.text: It was passed down to me from King to King. It belonged to Oaknock. He proclaimed that only a hero of the gnomes should have it. I think you count as a hero. Also since you have been looking into Oaknock you

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.speaker: King Narnode Shareen
assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.text: might be able to work out what it is.
King Narnode gives you a small crystal seed.

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.player: Hmm I wonder what it does?

assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.speaker: King Narnode Shareen
assassination-talking-to-narnode-again-2.text: Well, I'm sure that your magical research skills will help you there. Good luck!
Congratulations, you've completed a quest: The Eyes of Glouphrie

1675-y.speaker: Brimstail
1675-y.text: Well, have a careful look around at everything in the next cave and come back and tell me what you find.

DwqU9V.player: Actually, I'm a bit busy right now.
